subject: P013 v0 of the flat-noise calibration bank: sample 11, origkey 24, voice keys 24-84, note 24 (root-matched, nothing resampled), amp and filter envelopes flat rectangles, Q 0, filter type LP2
method: H(f) = S(f)/S_open(f) with the open reference at FMORPH 251 and the SAME filter type; corner = highest frequency still within 3 dB of the passband (passband taken as the median of H over 110-240 Hz)
FILTER_TYPE_DEPENDENT: This is LP2. LP4 and LP6 give systematically LOWER corners at the same byte (at FMORPH 50: LP2 287.1, LP4 257.8, LP6 246.1 Hz). Do not apply this map to another filter type.
NOT_IN_FIRMWARE: RESOLUTION_NOTES 128. No per-byte cutoff table exists in the decompressed EOS 4.70 image: 3336 strictly ascending 256-entry runs were fitted against these points in log space and the best was rms 0.069 in ln at slope 2.04, i.e. nothing. Filter cutoff is done in E-mu's filter hardware, not in OS software, so unlike the envelope rate law this one can only ever be measured.
NOT_A_SINGLE_EXPONENTIAL: log-slope per byte is ~0.013-0.016 through the middle and accelerates above byte 180 (0.0207, 0.0259, 0.0300 over the last three segments). The panel reads 18334 Hz at FMORPH 251, which needs ~0.051/byte from 235.

panel_reference.note: read off the front panel by Jan, not measured from audio
